A15: Usage receipts are explicitly submitted to one repository-bound Work Item before it is closed, including while archived but not yet closed, only through a currently admitted Runtime-native Rust record call. Each append binds repositoryId, workItemId, sourceEventId, sourceKind (provider-reported/host-reported/agent-declared), actor or explicit unknown, configuredModel, reportedModel, role, phase, non-overlapping unit (invocation or turn), nullable inputTokens/outputTokens/cachedInputTokens/reasoningTokens, sourceObservedAt, Runtime receivedAt, and evidence digest/ref. The sourceKind label is a caller claim, not authentication: self-reported provider/host labels and reportedModel never become verified host measurements merely by their wording or digest. Only an independently verified supported adapter/evidence route may raise provenance assurance; digest proves byte binding only. Model and token-count provenance remain separate. Replaying the same (repositoryId, workItemId, sourceKind, sourceEventId) with identical content is idempotent; conflicting content, cross-Work-Item binding, overflow, or invalid subset totals is rejected. Ordinary recording after close is rejected. Only explicit admitted record calls write usage receipts; query does not, and no provider credentials or background collection are introduced.

A16: Token counts are u64-or-null; null means unknown and is never rendered as zero. cachedInputTokens is a subset of inputTokens and reasoningTokens is a subset of outputTokens; subsets are never counted twice. Query model filtering uses actual reportedModel, with configuredModel separately retained. Provenance and assurance for model identity and token counts are independently represented; an agent-declared or caller-labeled reportedModel is not described as host-observed, and a sourceKind value alone never raises assurance. sourceObservedAt is accepted only with an explicit RFC3339 offset and trusted source provenance; otherwise it is unknown. Runtime receivedAt is separate. Cumulative counters that cannot be safely differenced produce partial/unknown coverage, not estimates. A content digest establishes bytes and identity binding, not the accuracy of self-declared fields.

A17: TaskOutcomeReport usage is optional only when decoding historical pre-feature reports. Every newly generated finish or terminal report durably includes a usage state, receipt refs/digests, per-reported-model/role/phase subtotals when known, coverage, and an explicit cutoff. With no usage receipts, coverage is unknown, token counts are null, and a reason is recorded; the field is not omitted and counts are never zero-filled. Summary and full Outcome views in English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese show coverage, unknown reason, and cutoff. Missing or unknown usage does not fail software verification. Read-only query/export expose safe receipt refs/digests and metadata without writing receipts or returning raw payloads by default.

A18: Finish freezes its cutoff-bound usage snapshot and report bytes; archive preserves those report bytes. Until close, an admitted explicit usage record may append to the same Work Item, including when archived but not yet closed, without modifying the finish report or archive. Close creates a distinct finalReport referencing all usage receipts received by its explicit close cutoff; it does not rewrite earlier reports. Ordinary recording after close is rejected. Final replies or usage not yet reported by the close cutoff remain partial/unknown and cannot be claimed as a complete Work Item total. Historical reports without the optional usage field remain readable and byte-identical. Audit query page subtotals are page-scoped, never whole-Work-Item totals.

changes.value: A19: Runtime reads its execution machine clock at the successful lifecycle transition and stores UTC RFC3339. Start, finish, archive, and close are separate observed facts, each with occurredAt and recordedAt plus event type, actor provenance, receipt refs, and digest. A terminal transition not yet reached is null; a historical missing fact is explicitly unknown and never inferred from scaffold createdAt, mtime, or unrelated evidence. For external usage/CI facts, sourceObservedAt and Runtime receivedAt remain separate. Process elapsedMs uses a monotonic clock and is kept distinct from Work Item wallElapsed, which spans observed start to terminal close, includes waiting, and is never calculated by summing verification nodes. Missing external offsets/unreliable sources, cross-host negative intervals, or clock anomalies are unknown/anomalous rather than fabricated precision. Human-readable Outcome/query output names its IANA timezone; the requested view uses Asia/Tokyo without changing host/system TZ, backed by the scoped IANA timezone database dependency rather than hand-written DST rules.

changes.value: A12: Composition attempts separate execution outcome, execution-evidence completeness, supervisor ownership/termination proof, and cleanup disposition. After the command result is durably captured, the exact owner identity and all owned descendants are fully reaped to waitpid ECHILD, and the bound supervisor receipt is coherent, a later external `verifier_process_using_worktree` observation error in `run_composition_inner` does not erase the observed command result: preserve executionOutcome as passed/failed and executionEvidenceComplete=true, set cleanupDisposition=deferred, and retain the worktree plus registration. This observer error never authorizes cleanup or terminal reuse. If owned termination proof, exact command result, receipt durability, or generation coherence is missing, remain unknown/retained and fail closed. Legacy v1/v2 attempts without owner and termination proof remain unknown. Linux receipts bind schema, attemptId, runNonce/generation, owner/supervisor identities, Linux boot/environment identity, Runtime identity, repository/target/snapshot, command plan, input environment, and ordered execution-record digest. Enforce spawn→ready→durable registration/fsync→release; stop new spawns on revocation/completion, reap descendants to ECHILD, and durably persist receipts. EOF, leader exit, heartbeat, or a successful external cwd scan alone is insufficient. Crash or concurrent generation change fails closed; non-Linux behavior remains compatible.

A13: A deferred retry requires a current coherent receipt, exact owner/termination proof for the prior owned tree, exact command/source binding, current trusted policy, fresh ordinary admission, and the existing concrete side-effect-safe/no-op policy. Path location alone never proves isolation. A pure external observation error may defer cleanup and retain the prior path without discarding execution facts; a fresh retry is allowed only under the protected no-op policy after owned termination proof, uses a second formal `run_admitted_composition` call with a fresh attempt/nonce/worktree, reuses no prior result, and leaves the old directory untouched. Confirmed active use, unknown or incomplete owned termination, stale generation/binding, unknown command effects, or denied admission blocks before spawn. Tests inject the external observer error only at the cleanup-decision boundary and assert retained path/registration; they separately prove a safe fresh no-op retry and that active/unknown owned trees remain blocked.

value.expected: When exact command result and owned-tree ECHILD termination are durable, an external `/proc/<pid>/cwd` observer error yields deferred cleanup and retained directory/registration without changing execution passed/failed or evidence completeness.
value.verificationPlan: Inject observer Err at the narrow cleanup-decision seam in `run_composition_inner`; assert exact execution outcome/completeness, deferred disposition, and untouched worktree plus registration. Also assert missing owner/reap proof remains unknown and retained.

value.expected: With a current protected no-op policy and prior owned termination proof, a fresh admitted composition can retry after external observation uncertainty without deleting or reusing the old path; active/unknown owned tree remains blocked.
value.verificationPlan: Call `run_admitted_composition` twice under the current safe no-op strategy; first call records completed execution plus deferred cleanup under injected observer Err, second receives fresh attempt/nonce/worktree, reuses no result, preserves old directory, and succeeds. Add denied/active/unknown-owned-tree cases asserting zero second verifier spawns. Keep this distinct from `repeated_exact_composition_reuses_only_when_inputs_are_observable` and `node_without_observable_inputs_executes_again_instead_of_reusing`.

A10: Linux records the process-group leader identity at activation (PID, starttime, PGID, SID) and reconciles only against that generation. Treat the group as exited only after a complete, bounded, repeatable /proc scan finds no members or finds only Z/X members with a stable identical (PID,starttime,PGID) set, a matching leader identity, and an unchanged latest-attempt digest before cleanup. Any non-Z/X member is active. Missing/inconsistent leader identity while members remain, PID reuse, attempt-state change, scan race, proc read/parse/permission failure, or budget exhaustion is unknown and preserves the worktree. A11: Run the Linux zombie-only process-group regression as an independent acceptance check, separate from the hosted package-coverage check. A12: Composition attempts distinguish execution outcome from cleanup disposition. The v3 attempt records executionOutcome (passed/failed/unknown), executionEvidenceComplete, backend-tagged supervisorReceipt, and cleanup disposition (cleaned/deferred/retained/failed/unknown). A v3 execution pass is not proof of cleanup or reuse. Strict terminal reuse requires coherent complete execution evidence and verified cleanup. Legacy v1/v2 attempts without ownership and termination proof remain unknown and cannot authorize reuse or retry. Linux receipts bind schema, attemptId, runNonce/generation, owner and supervisor process identities, Linux boot/environment identity, Runtime identity, repository/target/snapshot, command plan, input environment, and ordered execution-record digest. Path location alone never proves isolation. Otherwise, unknown owner/tree/effects/command source, stale binding/generation, or denied admission blocks before spawn. A safe retry uses a second formal run_admitted_composition call to create a fresh attempt, nonce, and worktree; it reuses no prior result and leaves the old deferred directory untouched. Regression coverage must make two consecutive formal calls: the first execution passes with deferred cleanup; the second safe fresh attempt succeeds while the old directory remains.

acceptanceCriteria: A1: Preserve the exact original 16 stable-release product paths and stable SemVer 1.0.1 invariants. The only additional product/source/test paths are the paths explicitly declared in Contract.scope for the already-scoped Linux composition supervisor/attempt/reconciliation correction, usage receipts and Outcome projection, lifecycle/audit read/query/export, timezone rendering, CLI/MCP parity, and deterministic Linux/query/export/help regression coverage. The only additional documentation projections are the declared collaboration language/scenario matrix and usage, lifecycle, audit, and command-reference pages. No other product/source/test or documentation paths change. The original Work Item, parity, and generated command-reference pages remain protocol projections. Historical v1.0.0 and v1.0.1-rc.2 identities remain separate.

A2: The stable v1.0.1 source and the scoped Linux process-supervision/retry correction have an independent technical review with no blocking product-code findings; attribute that conclusion to its actual reviewer (agent:Raydot), not human:Ray, and bind the review to the exact candidate head.

A3: Before any tag is created, a Runtime-bound release plan consumes fresh evidence for the exact current source/PR, confirms the existing public stable v1.0.0 tag and Release are the selected no-write N-1 reference, confirms the v1.0.1 tag and Release names are unused, records the provider's actual immutability metadata without overstating it, and confirms the existing workflow gates public Release publication on candidate checks.

After normal PR merge and fresh Runtime publication admission only, create the new immutable v1.0.1 tag on the accepted merge commit. The existing workflow must build and pass candidate install/smoke for aarch64-apple-darwin (Homebrew), x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and staged full N-1 upgrade from stable v1.0.0 must pass on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu before public Release publication. Do not substitute N/A or another predecessor.

After public Release publication, download the official manifest, SHA256SUMS, and Linux x86_64 artifact; verify their identities and digests and pass public install plus N-1 upgrade from v1.0.0 with post-upgrade checks. Preserve any failure and never replace existing immutable assets.

On the local Apple Silicon macOS host, install the published macOS binary at the declared absolute path and update the CLI/MCP executable binding. Verify that official archive/manifest/SHA256SUMS agree, record the actual installed binary SHA-256 and version 1.0.1, confirm CLI absolute path and MCP initialize plus read-only request. Check a local build only for source/provenance/version; do not require its binary hash to equal the official artifact or mutate provider-global identity configuration.

After every release acceptance step succeeds, Runtime admits cleanup and close, and the exact merged PR branch/worktree cleanup plus final lifecycle receipts are recorded. No tag, release, or asset is overwritten or deleted.

Before marking PR #1022 ready or performing its normal merge, GitHub Actions must be fully successful for the exact current PR head after Runtime admits its hosted Work Item verification. This includes all required route, quality, Rust Contract, repository-gate and 13-package coverage, Windows Runtime, and behavioral-oracle checks. Preserve failed attempts; a changed head requires new exact-head CI.

A10: Linux records the process-group leader identity at activation (PID, starttime, PGID, SID) and reconciles only against that generation. Treat the group as exited only after a complete, bounded, repeatable /proc scan finds no members or finds only Z/X members with a stable identical (PID,starttime,PGID) set, a matching leader identity, and an unchanged latest-attempt digest before cleanup. Any non-Z/X member is active. Missing/inconsistent leader identity while members remain, PID reuse, attempt-state change, scan race, proc read/parse/permission failure, or budget exhaustion is unknown and preserves the worktree. Preserve the existing cwd/open-file verifier check; no per-stateDir single-writer assumption; non-Linux behavior is unchanged. Deterministic tests cover zombie-only, mixed zombie/live, live then killed/reaped, injected malformed/unreadable/identity-change/budget cases; the fixture retains zombie state with WNOWAIT and reaps its own child after assertions, never relying on PID 1.

A11: Run the Linux zombie-only process-group regression as an independent acceptance check, separate from the hosted package-coverage check. Preserve its exact command, exit status, candidate head, Contract digest, snapshot digest, and output as separate acceptance evidence. Keep Contract.verification to the single unfiltered command cargo test --locked --workspace; do not place the targeted Cargo test there because the hosted consumer requires a unique complete workspace-test declaration.

A12: Composition attempts separate execution outcome, execution-evidence completeness, supervisor ownership/termination proof, and cleanup disposition. After the command result is durably captured, the exact owner identity and all owned descendants are fully reaped to waitpid ECHILD, and the bound supervisor receipt is coherent, a later external `verifier_process_using_worktree` observation error in `run_composition_inner` does not erase the observed command result: preserve executionOutcome as passed/failed and executionEvidenceComplete=true, set cleanupDisposition=deferred, and retain the worktree plus registration. This observer error never authorizes cleanup or terminal reuse. If owned termination proof, exact command result, receipt durability, or generation coherence is missing, remain unknown/retained and fail closed. Legacy v1/v2 attempts without owner and termination proof remain unknown. Linux receipts bind schema, attemptId, runNonce/generation, owner/supervisor identities, Linux boot/environment identity, Runtime identity, repository/target/snapshot, command plan, input environment, and ordered execution-record digest. Enforce spawn→ready→durable registration/fsync→release; stop new spawns on revocation/completion, reap descendants to ECHILD, and durably persist receipts. EOF, leader exit, heartbeat, or a successful external cwd scan alone is insufficient. Crash or concurrent generation change fails closed; non-Linux behavior remains compatible.

A13: A deferred retry requires a current coherent receipt, exact owner/termination proof for the prior owned tree, exact command/source binding, current trusted policy, fresh ordinary admission, and the existing concrete side-effect-safe/no-op policy. Path location alone never proves isolation. A pure external observation error may defer cleanup and retain the prior path without discarding execution facts; a fresh retry is allowed only under the protected no-op policy after owned termination proof, uses a second formal `run_admitted_composition` call with a fresh attempt/nonce/worktree, reuses no prior result, and leaves the old directory untouched. Confirmed active use, unknown or incomplete owned termination, stale generation/binding, unknown command effects, or denied admission blocks before spawn. Tests inject the external observer error only at the cleanup-decision boundary and assert retained path/registration; they separately prove a safe fresh no-op retry and that active/unknown owned trees remain blocked.

A14: Use the approved hidden ai-cockpit internal composition supervisor entry in the existing crates/cockpit-cli/src/main.rs; do not add an implicit module or new binary. crates/cockpit-mcp/src/lib.rs must use the exact Runtime helper identity; library tests use a controlled test helper, with no PATH guessing. Every actual verifier spawn still passes through ProcessStartGate; helper IPC errors or admission revocation produce zero verifier spawns. Keep execution, cleanup, projection, and lifecycle state distinct. After composition, a separate current-receipt verify and green preflight remain required before finish.

A15: Usage receipts are explicitly submitted to one repository-bound Work Item before it is closed, including while archived but not yet closed, only through a currently admitted Runtime-native Rust record call. Each append binds repositoryId, workItemId, sourceEventId, sourceKind (provider-reported/host-reported/agent-declared), actor or explicit unknown, configuredModel, reportedModel, role, phase, non-overlapping unit (invocation or turn), nullable inputTokens/outputTokens/cachedInputTokens/reasoningTokens, sourceObservedAt, Runtime receivedAt, and evidence digest/ref. The sourceKind label is a caller claim, not authentication: self-reported provider/host labels and reportedModel never become verified host measurements merely by their wording or digest. Only an independently verified supported adapter/evidence route may raise provenance assurance; digest proves byte binding only. Model and token-count provenance remain separate. Replaying the same (repositoryId, workItemId, sourceKind, sourceEventId) with identical content is idempotent; conflicting content, cross-Work-Item binding, overflow, or invalid subset totals is rejected. Ordinary recording after close is rejected. Only explicit admitted record calls write usage receipts; query does not, and no provider credentials or background collection are introduced.

A16: Token counts are u64-or-null; null means unknown and is never rendered as zero. cachedInputTokens is a subset of inputTokens and reasoningTokens is a subset of outputTokens; subsets are never counted twice. Query model filtering uses actual reportedModel, with configuredModel separately retained. Provenance and assurance for model identity and token counts are independently represented; an agent-declared or caller-labeled reportedModel is not described as host-observed, and a sourceKind value alone never raises assurance. sourceObservedAt is accepted only with an explicit RFC3339 offset and trusted source provenance; otherwise it is unknown. Runtime receivedAt is separate. Cumulative counters that cannot be safely differenced produce partial/unknown coverage, not estimates. A content digest establishes bytes and identity binding, not the accuracy of self-declared fields.

A17: TaskOutcomeReport usage is optional only when decoding historical pre-feature reports. Every newly generated finish or terminal report durably includes a usage state, receipt refs/digests, per-reported-model/role/phase subtotals when known, coverage, and an explicit cutoff. With no usage receipts, coverage is unknown, token counts are null, and a reason is recorded; the field is not omitted and counts are never zero-filled. Summary and full Outcome views in English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese show coverage, unknown reason, and cutoff. Missing or unknown usage does not fail software verification. Read-only query/export expose safe receipt refs/digests and metadata without writing receipts or returning raw payloads by default.

A18: Finish freezes its cutoff-bound usage snapshot and report bytes; archive preserves those report bytes. Until close, an admitted explicit usage record may append to the same Work Item, including when archived but not yet closed, without modifying the finish report or archive. Close creates a distinct finalReport referencing all usage receipts received by its explicit close cutoff; it does not rewrite earlier reports. Ordinary recording after close is rejected. Final replies or usage not yet reported by the close cutoff remain partial/unknown and cannot be claimed as a complete Work Item total. Historical reports without the optional usage field remain readable and byte-identical. Audit query page subtotals are page-scoped, never whole-Work-Item totals.

A19: Runtime reads its execution machine clock at the successful lifecycle transition and stores UTC RFC3339. Start, finish, archive, and close are separate observed facts, each with occurredAt and recordedAt plus event type, actor provenance, receipt refs, and digest. A terminal transition not yet reached is null; a historical missing fact is explicitly unknown and never inferred from scaffold createdAt, mtime, or unrelated evidence. For external usage/CI facts, sourceObservedAt and Runtime receivedAt remain separate. Process elapsedMs uses a monotonic clock and is kept distinct from Work Item wallElapsed, which spans observed start to terminal close, includes waiting, and is never calculated by summing verification nodes. Missing external offsets/unreliable sources, cross-host negative intervals, or clock anomalies are unknown/anomalous rather than fabricated precision. Human-readable Outcome/query output names its IANA timezone; the requested view uses Asia/Tokyo without changing host/system TZ, backed by the scoped IANA timezone database dependency rather than hand-written DST rules.

A20: Reuse current repository-bound AuditEvent/export and existing lifecycle/authorization/verification/release/recovery/cleanup/close evidence as the fact source; do not add a second fact store, SIEM, full logging service, or claim local export is immutable external retention. Lifecycle event rows bind repository, Work Item, Runtime identity, event type, actor provenance (or unknown), actual UTC timestamp, source evidence digest, and refs. An interval is labeled wall-clock elapsed, never active execution or thinking time.

A21: Add typed read-only ai-cockpit audit query and MCP audit_query backed by one shared Rust protocol/repository read service over existing .ai/evidence and AuditEvent sources. Exact filters are Work Item ID, inclusive from and exclusive to RFC3339 bounds applied only to Runtime recordedAt, actual reported model, actor, event type, limit (1..=100; default 50), opaque cursor, and optional IANA displayTimezone. No fallback from missing recordedAt to occurredAt, sourceObservedAt, receivedAt, createdAt, or mtime is allowed; unknown timestamps remain explicit coverage gaps while their source fields are preserved for inspection. Results use a stable order with eventID as tie-break. The structured page includes schemaVersion, repositoryId, Runtime version/digest, canonical UTC asOf, sourceSnapshotDigest, normalized filters, items with event identity/type, Work Item, occurredAt/recordedAt/sourceObservedAt/receivedAt, reportedModel/configuredModel, actor, nullable token counts and receipt refs/digests, coverage (complete/partial/unknown plus knownCount, nullable unknownCount when indeterminate, unknownSources/reasons), page-only usage subtotals, returnedCount, truncated, and nextCursor. Cursor binds filters, source snapshot, and stable ordering; changed sources reject with stale_cursor. Query writes no repository evidence, collects no secrets, uploads nothing, and returns no raw payloads.

A22: Extend `audit export` with the same typed filters, pagination, coverage, and snapshot behavior while keeping a no-filter invocation wire-compatible with the existing schema-v1 AuditExportManifest and preserving explicit local `--output` idempotency. Filtered export uses the shared query envelope; timestamps remain canonical UTC. MCP exposes `audit_query` through the same read service. Do not reuse generic raw `evidence_get` payloads as safe export. The shared reader regression uses the actual `{workItemId}.{digest}.delegated.json` filename and validates it against the parsed receipt identity; a mismatch is rejected, and any filename-derived binding defect is fixed only after that RED test demonstrates it.

A23: Before release, verify top-level/group/leaf/parameter `--help`, all three `docs/reference/commands.{md,zh-CN.md,ja.md}` command and MCP-tool tables, and actual MCP `initialize` plus `tools/list` schemas for `work-item usage record`, `audit query`, filtered `audit export`, and Outcome timezone display. Public help/docs/tool discovery contain no `__composition-supervisor`; its existing internal helper path remains separately exercised. Usage record/query/export and rendering are native Rust Runtime surfaces sharing protocol/repository services, never shell/Python helpers or chat-only bookkeeping. Preserve the existing hidden-helper identity and admission/security boundaries.
newContract.goal: Starting from main c417b65c3f3608b7fd2336314d7432fd72fa8723, make and verify the exact original 16-path stable v1.0.1 update and the already-scoped Linux-only zombie-only verifier process-group liveness correction; retain the unique full-workspace verification declaration and independent Linux regression evidence; implement opt-in repository-bound Work Item usage receipts, distinct Runtime-recorded start/finish/archive/close facts, a typed read-only audit query and MCP surface, filtered audit export that preserves the legacy unfiltered wire, accurate UTC/IANA-zone time rendering, and complete CLI/MCP discovery/docs; pass exact-head repository CI and release gates; prove candidate build/install smoke for Apple Silicon macOS Homebrew, Linux x86_64 GNU, Linux ARM64 GNU, and Windows x86_64 MSVC; run full N-1 acceptance only on Linux x86_64; verify local macOS CLI/MCP identity switching; then publish stable v1.0.1 only after Runtime-admitted review and current acceptance evidence. Do not overwrite any existing tag or immutable release asset.
newContract.intent: Prepare the existing v1.0.1 line as a genuine stable release rather than a prerelease, with corrected release identity and consistent localized version/distribution documentation. Add explicit auditable per-Work-Item token usage, provenance-preserving lifecycle timestamps, and a read-only filtered Runtime audit query/export in this same release. Reuse existing repository evidence and authorization, verification, release, recovery, cleanup, and close records; do not infer facts, collect provider secrets automatically, create another audit store, or rewrite history.
outOfScope: Any product/source/test or documentation path outside Contract.scope; changes to .github/workflows/release.yml absent a separately admitted demonstrated defect; editing or deleting historical failure evidence; merging before exact-head CI and required independent review; tagging or publishing before Contract review and candidate acceptance; inferring isolation from path location alone; PATH-based helper discovery or an unapproved helper module/new binary; process-global PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER changes; ignoring permission errors; TTL/forced deletion; Docker/unshare isolation; bypassing stateDir ownership or Runtime admission; reusing an old execution result on retry; overwriting any existing tag, Release, or immutable asset.
Billing, pricing, charge estimation, budgets, quotas, or spend controls.
Background usage collection, telemetry, provider credential/API setup, or reading sessions that the host or adapter denies.
Estimating token counts from elapsed time, message length, or configured model metadata.
Reopening a closed Work Item or mutating an immutable archive to backfill late usage.
A new SIEM, full event logging platform, or external WORM/retention service; continue to use the existing AuditEvent and audit export handoff.
Inferring a historical Work Item start from Contract createdAt, file modification times, or unrelated evidence timestamps.
Treating wall-clock elapsed time as active execution time, model-thinking time, or an estimate of token usage.
Automatic provider/model telemetry, API-key collection, or background usage polling; recording is explicit and uses only supplied source facts.
Including API keys, full environment snapshots, raw chain-of-thought, or full chat transcripts in default query/export; uploading audit/query results remotely.
Treating paged usage subtotals as whole-Work-Item totals or guessing timestamps, timezone offsets, source identity, active time, or token counts.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A successful execution with deferred cleanup records execution pass separately, preserves the owned directory, and is not classified as a cleaned reusable terminal attempt.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run a controlled formal composition whose command passes while cleanup is deferred; inspect the bound attempt receipt, projection, and preserved directory.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Two consecutive formal run_admitted_composition calls prove a safe second attempt gets a fresh nonce/worktree, reuses no old result, succeeds, and leaves the first deferred directory untouched.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use a first formal call that passes with deferred cleanup, then a second admitted formal call under current policy and exact command/source binding; compare attempt IDs, nonces, worktrees, results, and the old directory.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Unknown ownership, side effects, source/command binding, stale generation, or denied admission blocks a repeat before any verifier spawn and preserves existing data.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inject each unsafe or unknown precondition; assert admission rejection, zero verifier spawns, preserved deferred path, and retained failure evidence.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Backend-tagged supervisor receipt requirements do not break supported non-Linux composition behavior.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the controlled non-Linux backend coverage and confirm Linux-only identity fields are not required outside Linux while shared execution/cleanup semantics remain coherent.

scenarioCoverage.expected: CLI and MCP use the exact Runtime helper identity and agree on attempt, execution, cleanup, and admission outcomes.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Exercise the hidden CLI supervisor entry and MCP route with controlled helpers; compare serialized receipts/projections and assert PATH lookup is not used.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A composition result alone cannot finish WI-1068; a separate current-receipt verification and green preflight are required.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Show finish remains inadmissible after composition alone, then bind independent current verify and green preflight evidence before the finish gate can admit.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A recorded usage receipt is projected in Outcome; absent or incomplete data is displayed as unknown/partial and does not fail software verification.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Exercise explicit repository recording and every new finish/terminal TaskOutcomeReport projection with present, absent, nullable, and partial fields; no receipts must persist coverage unknown, null counts, and a reason rather than omit usage or write zero. Confirm query does not create a receipt and software verification is unchanged.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Different reported/configured models, sources, roles, and phases remain distinct; cached/reasoning subsets do not double count and unknown remains null.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Record multiple explicit invocation/turn units and assert exact per-dimension subtotals, subset bounds, no double counting, and partial coverage for non-differentiable cumulative data. Keep model-identity provenance separate from token-count provenance; caller-labeled provider/host and reportedModel remain self-declared unless a supported adapter independently verifies them.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Replaying the same sourceEventID and identical payload is idempotent; a conflicting payload and cross-Work-Item event are rejected without changing prior receipts.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Submit identical, conflicting, and cross-WI event IDs; compare append-only receipt bytes, sequence, and digest before and after each request.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Pre-feature TaskOutcomeReport/archive records decode without usage and their archived bytes remain unchanged.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Load existing report fixtures with no usage field, render them, and verify archive integrity and original byte digests.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Finish/close captures a bound cutoff and usage snapshot; no post-close mutation or retroactive archive edit occurs, and missing late data remains partial/unknown.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Record usage before finish and verify the frozen report cutoff and archive bytes. Record additional usage through current Runtime admission after archive but before close, and assert finish/archive digests remain unchanged while close creates a distinct finalReport referencing receipts received by its explicit close cutoff. Reject ordinary post-close recording; final reply or missing late data remains partial/unknown, never a complete total.

scenarioCoverage.expected: CLI and MCP usage-record entry points share repository semantics and return equivalent receipt identities, digests, idempotency, and rejection outcomes.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run paired CLI/MCP requests against the same repository service test fixture and compare normalized receipts and errors.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Runtime start/finish/archive/close facts are separate UTC RFC3339 events with occurredAt/recordedAt and source refs; unfinished terminal times are null, historical missing values unknown, process duration monotonic, wall elapsed includes waiting, Tokyo rendering is explicit, and anomalies remain unknown.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Drive lifecycle actions through the Runtime service with an injectable clock; assert successful-action timestamps and evidence bindings, legacy missing facts, external offset/source handling, Asia/Tokyo formatting via IANA data, monotonic process elapsedMs, and cross-host/clock-anomaly unknown behavior without changing host TZ.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The existing AuditEvent/audit export and new typed query expose repository-bound start/finish/archive/close facts with timestamps, digests, refs, coverage, and cutoff; no second store is introduced.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Record and query lifecycle events using the same repository read service; test exact filters, page/cursor binding, source mutation to stale_cursor, exported references, and wall-clock labels.

scenarioCoverage.expected: CLI, MCP, and export share typed exact filters; UTC asOf/sourceSnapshotDigest, coverage/unknown, receipt refs, page-only usage totals, nextCursor, and stale_cursor behavior are consistent.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Query fixtures by Work Item, inclusive/exclusive RFC3339 bounds on Runtime recordedAt only, reported model, actor, and event; preserve other timestamp fields without fallback and mark unknown recordedAt coverage. Page with limit 1..=100 using stable eventID tie-break; assert returnedCount, truncated, nextCursor, nullable indeterminate unknownCount; mutate a source before the next cursor, compare CLI/MCP envelopes, and assert stale_cursor.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The existing no-filter audit export retains its schema-v1 wire shape and explicit local output behavior; filtered export uses the shared query envelope.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Compare no-filter export JSON and digest to a pre-feature fixture; verify identical --output is idempotent and conflicting bytes fail; then compare filtered CLI/MCP query results.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A receipt stored as `{workItemId}.{digest}.delegated.json` is attributed to the parsed repository-bound Work Item ID; mismatched path/receipt binding fails closed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create the valid receipt using the existing writer, feed it to the same shared audit reader used by export/query, assert the event has exactly receipt.workItemId, then alter the path or receipt identity and assert rejection. Apply only the minimal source fix if the first case is RED.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Rust Runtime CLI help, three-language command/MCP tables, MCP initialize/tools/list, and schemas expose usage record, audit query, and filtered export completely while the supervisor helper remains hidden.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run top-level, group, leaf, and parameter help snapshots; compare English/Simplified Chinese/Japanese command and MCP tables with actual CLI parser and tools/list; assert __composition-supervisor is absent publicly and the existing internal test route remains callable.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The existing Linux-only zombie group fix passes its independent targeted regression; live/mixed groups and procfs uncertainty remain fail-closed; no non-Linux behavior changes and older failure receipts remain intact.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use the exact independent command declared by A11, bind exit code/output to exact candidate and Contract/snapshot digests, separately run the unique workspace declaration only when formally admitted, and preserve all existing red evidence.

scenarioCoverage.expected: When exact command result and owned-tree ECHILD termination are durable, an external `/proc/<pid>/cwd` observer error yields deferred cleanup and retained directory/registration without changing execution passed/failed or evidence completeness.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inject observer Err at the narrow cleanup-decision seam in `run_composition_inner`; assert exact execution outcome/completeness, deferred disposition, and untouched worktree plus registration. Also assert missing owner/reap proof remains unknown and retained.

scenarioCoverage.expected: With a current protected no-op policy and prior owned termination proof, a fresh admitted composition can retry after external observation uncertainty without deleting or reusing the old path; active/unknown owned tree remains blocked.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Call `run_admitted_composition` twice under the current safe no-op strategy; first call records completed execution plus deferred cleanup under injected observer Err, second receives fresh attempt/nonce/worktree, reuses no result, preserves old directory, and succeeds. Add denied/active/unknown-owned-tree cases asserting zero second verifier spawns. Keep this distinct from `repeated_exact_composition_reuses_only_when_inputs_are_observable` and `node_without_observable_inputs_executes_again_instead_of_reusing`.
